upsertSlices.label: LCA; direct line-graph oracle baseline
upsertSlices.task: One color per queried edge, with all answers consistent with one proper coloring of G
assumptions: Direct line-graph oracle supplied; creating or simulating it from an ordinary adjacency-list or adjacency-matrix representation of G is outside this probe count
Simple graph; maximum line-graph degree D≥2; trivial D<2 cases are omitted
Use one fixed identifier assignment, oracle ordering and degree/size parameters for every query
Deterministic oblivious LCA; no stored state between queries
The resource is input probes per edge-color query, not total time or total cost for explicitly outputting every edge color

yAxis.label: Line-graph oracle probes per edge-color query; symbolic category

parameters.m: Number of edges of G, equivalently number of vertices of L(G)
parameters.Delta: Maximum degree of the original graph G

results.bound: D^{O(√D log^{5/2}D)} · log* m line-graph oracle probes per queried edge
results.guarantee: Proper edge coloring from a palette of D+1 colors, at most 2Δ−1
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 5.1 (second case), Section 5; l=D+1 and d=1 on L(G)
results.notes: A direct theorem specialization, not an author-stated edge-LCA optimum. D is the degree of the line graph, not the degree Δ of G. The numerical exponent hidden in O(·) is not specified. The reviewed source provides no matching edge-LCA lower bound for this oracle. Direct oracle access to vertices and neighborhoods of L(G), using the probe convention of Theorem 5.1; line-graph vertices are identified original edges
